title: decision: FramedContentTBS carries the semiprivate wire format, not PrivateMessage's
description:
Mark 2026-11-26. semiprivatemessage-08 §3.1 says
`framed_content_tbs_hash = hash(FramedContentTBS)`, and RFC 9420 §6.1's
FramedContentTBS has a `WireFormat wire_format` field. The draft never
says which value goes in it for a SemiPrivateMessage, and it has to,
because the hash and the signature both cover it.

## The readings

1. `mls_semiprivate_message` (TBD1, suggested 0x0011), the format the
   message is actually in. Chosen.
2. `mls_private_message` (0x0003), on the grounds that §3 describes
   SemiPrivateMessage as extending PrivateMessage and §3.2 says the
   member's path works "just as for a PrivateMessage".

## Why the message's own format

RFC 9420 §6.1 puts wire_format in FramedContentTBS so the signature
binds the framing. Reading 2 breaks that: a SemiPrivateMessage and a
PrivateMessage carrying the same FramedContent would have the same
signature, so either could be repackaged as the other and still verify.
The draft adds a wire format precisely so a group can require
SemiPrivateMessage (§3 L173-179); a signature that does not distinguish
it from PrivateMessage would let a sender satisfy that requirement with
a message the external receivers cannot read, and let anyone strip the
external receivers back off.

Reading 2's textual support is about the key schedule and the sender
data, which genuinely are PrivateMessage's. It says nothing about the
signature's inputs.

## Cost if this is wrong

Interop, not security. A sender using the other value produces a
signature and a hash that mimid rejects, visibly, on the first
handshake. Reading 1 is also the stricter of the two, so a mimid that
guesses wrong refuses messages rather than accepting forged ones.

## Also unstated, and recorded here

An external receiver has to reconstruct FramedContent to recompute the
hash, and FramedContent carries the sender. The frame does not give it
in the clear: a member reads it from the decrypted SenderData, which an
external receiver has no key for. The sender_leaf_index inside
PerMessageKeyAndNonces is what fills that gap, which is presumably why
the field is there -- the draft does not say so, and §3.3 mentions it
only as an input to partial_context_hash.

Both points are items 9 and 10 for bead mimid-1wgh.44.22.
